question: Fed Decision in September?
resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

# Fed September 2026 decision: research summary (as of 2026-08-30)

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding source is the FOMC statement from the September 15-16, 2026 meeting, measured by the upper bound of the target range. The Fed's open market page is a secondary reference. [Fed open market page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm)
- 2025-12-10/11: the last change before the cutoff was a 25 bp cut, which set the range at 3.50-3.75%. The upper bound is **3.75%**. [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm)
- 2026-07-29: the FOMC voted 9-3 to keep the range at 3.50-3.75%. This was the fifth hold in a row. [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/sca-en/market-analysis/news-and-research/breaking-fed-keeps-rates-unchanged-amid-regional-dissents-and-warsh-s-pause), [Wolf Street](https://wolfstreet.com/2026/07/29/fed-holds-rates-after-good-family-fight-with-3-dissenters-after-enormous-uncertainty-in-the-markets/)
- Note: some pages I fetched were updated after 2026-08-30. I ignored that content, as instructed.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing had settled the question by 2026-08-30. The meeting is on Sept 15-16. Before the cutoff, markets saw a 25 bp hike against no change as roughly a coin flip. A cut was not being seriously priced.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-28: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh gave the Jackson Hole keynote and said he was committed to fighting inflation. He said that "while this summer's readings were better than expected," they don't show the underlying trend has meaningfully improved, and that the Fed must be confident inflation is heading to 2% or "we have work to do." After the speech the 2-year Treasury yield hit its highest level since late July. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)
- 2026-08-12: July CPI rose 0.1% for the month and 3.4% from a year earlier, down from 3.5% in June and in line with consensus. Core CPI rose 0.2% for the month. Baird's Donald Rissmiller wrote: "nothing in today's CPI report that demands a September rate hike." After the release, the odds of a September hike fell. [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/cpi-inflation-july-2026), [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/economy/middle-road-july-cpi-likely-gives-fed-breathing-room-rate-hikes)
- 2026-08-07: the July jobs report unexpectedly showed the US lost jobs. CME odds of a September hold rose to 60%, from 45% the day before. Futures still priced about 55% for an October hike and about 75% for a hike by December. In June, prices had their biggest monthly drop in six years because energy prices fell, and oil then rose in July on Middle East tensions. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html)
- 2026-07-29: at the July meeting, Hammack, Kashkari and Logan all dissented in favor of a hike. The statement was short and gave no forward guidance. Warsh called this a "period of watchful thinking" and said rising bond yields reflected a strong economy. [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/sca-en/market-analysis/news-and-research/breaking-fed-keeps-rates-unchanged-amid-regional-dissents-and-warsh-s-pause), [MUFG](https://mufgresearch.com/rates/july-2026-fomc-recap/)

## 4. Base rates
- The range has not changed since December 2025, so five meetings in a row ended in a hold (January through July 2026). [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/sca-en/market-analysis/news-and-research/breaking-fed-keeps-rates-unchanged-amid-regional-dissents-and-warsh-s-pause)
- The last three changes were 25 bp cuts in September, October and December 2025. [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm)
- Historically, the Fed almost always moves in 25 bp steps. Moves of 50 bp or more are rare and usually happen during crises. The Fed seldom acts against market pricing that is clearly one-sided, but pricing here is close to 50/50.
- The policy direction has turned from cuts to possible hikes: the dissents are hawkish and futures price hikes later in 2026.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-28: after the Warsh speech, CME FedWatch showed about 56% for a 25 bp hike in September. Kalshi showed 48% for a hike, down from about 70% for a hold before the speech. Polymarket showed 49% for a hike. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)
- 2026-08-07: CME showed 60% for a hold, Kalshi 65% for a hold. Just after the July meeting, Kalshi had shown about 58% for a hike. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html)
- I found no meaningful market pricing for a cut or for a hike of 50 bp or more.
- I left out a Forbes piece putting the CME hike probability at 66% because it is dated 2026-08-31, after the cutoff.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-09-04: the August jobs report. After July's job losses, this is the key labor reading.
- About 2026-09-10/11: August CPI and PPI.
- Through the blackout period, which starts about 2026-09-05: Fed officials' speeches. The hawkish regional presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) and Warsh's framing are the ones to watch.
- Oil and Middle East developments that affect headline inflation.
- 2026-09-16: the FOMC statement, Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot) and Warsh's press conference.

I could not confirm the exact July payroll number or the August PCE figures.

Sources: [Fed open market page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), [CNBC 08-28](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html), [CNBC 08-07](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html), [XTB](https://www.xtb.com/sca-en/market-analysis/news-and-research/breaking-fed-keeps-rates-unchanged-amid-regional-dissents-and-warsh-s-pause), [Wolf Street](https://wolfstreet.com/2026/07/29/fed-holds-rates-after-good-family-fight-with-3-dissenters-after-enormous-uncertainty-in-the-markets/), [MUFG](https://mufgresearch.com/rates/july-2026-fomc-recap/), [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/cpi-inflation-july-2026), [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/economy/middle-road-july-cpi-likely-gives-fed-breathing-room-rate-hikes)
